text:
Maya: Heads-up — we've got an edge case: route-based cost shielding is causing permission mismatches. Canary routing tries to pick the 'opt-cheap' variant but that variant isn't allowed by the tenant's role scopes, so requests end up 403-ing.
Sam: Oof. Where's the denial happening — router or authz service? Any example logs?
Maya: Router picks variant first, then authz rejects when we validate model access. Example log: `router: chose variant=opt-cheap -> authz: deny model_variant`
Li: Can we short-circuit and check authz at routing-decision time (before variant selection)? That should avoid wasted routing + request attempts.
Jonah: Careful — routing uses cost/latency heuristics and needs model profiles. Hitting authz synchronously in the decision path could add latency and an extra call per request.
Kavi: From console UX perspective: when rollout/canary doesn't shift as expected, operators need to know why. We should show an explicit reason like "variant filtered by permissions" in the rollout UI.
Maya: Agreed. Proposal outline: 1) compute allowed-variants per-tenant at config time (periodic job or on config change); 2) router consults cached allowed-variants when evaluating candidates; 3) fallback to next eligible variant if primary is disallowed; 4) surface counters and UI reasons.
Sam: Telemetry plan: emit `route_variant_permission_denied{route,variant,tenant}` counter + sample traces (one per affected request) so we can correlate user errors with rollout state. Also add an alert when denial rate > 1% for a route.
Li: For implementation, reusing scoped-token propagation and the existing authz cache seems best. We shouldn't add per-request synchronous authz calls. Instead maintain a small TTL'd allowed-variants cache derived from authz + model catalog.
Jonah: Agreed. Router change: consult allowed-variants cache in candidate filtering path. Cache invalidation is the tricky part — role changes must propagate quickly for enterprise customers.
Kavi: UX copy suggestion for the console: "Some variant candidates were removed by your org's role scopes. Update tenant roles or pin a different variant to resume traffic" — include a one-click link to open role edit.
Maya: Edge cases: 1) dynamic role changes -> cache stale; 2) multi-tenant routes where different orgs have different allowed sets; 3) default-fallback variants that are allowed but more expensive. We should emit audit events when allowed-variants change and show a timeline in the route dashboard.
Sam: For rollout safety, plan a phased deploy: router consults feature-flagged cache path behind FF, enable telemetry, run canary of router change in a single region, validate no latency regressions.
Maya: For the console, add a small indicator in the rollout flyout: "X variants filtered by permissions" with a hover listing tenants affected (sampled).
Li: Implementation tasks: metrics + trace sampling + cache builder + router integration. I'll own metrics/tracing.
Jonah: I'll own router cache integration and invalidation hook.
Kavi: I'll draft the UI copy + tooltip + flyout wireframe and add a screenshot to the rollout doc.
Maya: I'll create the PR template for the change and include the canary checklist. Who wants to pair on the initial router patch tomorrow morning? :eyes:
Jonah: I'll pair.
Li: I can be available for a telemetry sync afterwards.
Kavi: I'll review the UI in the afternoon.
deploy-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/router/pull/4567 — Maya, Jonah, Kavi assigned.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll update the rollout doc with the metric names and the console mock. Will follow up with a short doc for SRE about cache invalidation TTL recommendations.
